key_insight: Ba2La2MnTe2O12 shows unusually strong frustration and effectively ideal 2D antiferromagnetic order inside a 3D hexagonal perovskite, with 120° spins confined to the ab-plane and disordered along c.
engineering_relevance: This result highlights how lattice geometry and dimensionality can control emergent magnetic behavior, informing the design and interpretation of functional magnetic oxide materials.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a magnetic transition at T_N ≈ 4.4 K and supporting μSR evidence of persistent spin fluctuations and broad internal field distributions.
watch_item: The conclusion of ideal 2D magnetism is based on low-temperature probe data in one compound, so broader material claims should be validated case by case.
paper_title: Strongly frustrated 2D magnetism in a 3D hexagonal perovskite
